resources.string: Observes structural accessibility events only from TikTok, Instagram and YouTube to detect short-video transitions. Scroll Receipt does not read or store video text, captions, comments, messages, images, audio or screenshots.
Counting is automatic. You can close Scroll Receipt; the Android accessibility service keeps listening for supported short-video activity.
Enable the accessibility service once. After that, normal counting does not require a Start button.
Waiting for TikTok, Reels or Shorts

There is no Start button for normal use. Once Accessibility is enabled, Scroll Receipt receives supported Android UI events in the background and counts only when a short-video mode is recognized. Screen off, another app, comments/profile overlays and non-short modes are excluded by the detector.
This section does not start normal counting. Automatic measurement is already running. Use these buttons only to create a manual reference series and calculate detector error.
For 100 transitions this is usually 101 videos, including the first visible video.
Target app is not installed or cannot be launched. No diagnostic test was started.
This removes the local Gate 0A counters and diagnostic logs from this device.
Enter a positive manual count before finishing the test.
No network permission. No screenshots. No video content, captions, comments, messages, images or audio are stored. Gate 0A keeps only structural event metadata needed to validate the detector.
